assertion_results.text: The plan determines feature-branch workflow mode (not direct-to-main) based on the atomicity constraints in the feature description
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md states 'Selected mode: feature-branch' and lists three atomicity indicators: 'Coordinated schema migration', 'Breaking API changes', and 'Explicit atomicity requirement' with detailed justifications referencing the feature description's non-functional requirements about tightly coupled changes.

assertion_results.text: A bookend task with Bookend Type create-branch is generated as the first task in the plan
assertion_results.evidence: task-1-create-feature-branch.md contains '## Bookend Type\ncreate-branch' (lines 7-8). summary-comment.md confirms Task 1 is 'Bookend (create-branch)' and it is the first task in the table.

assertion_results.text: A bookend task with Bookend Type merge-branch is generated as the last task in the plan
assertion_results.evidence: task-8-merge-feature-branch.md contains '## Bookend Type\nmerge-branch' (lines 7-8). summary-comment.md confirms Task 8 is 'Bookend (merge-branch)' and it is the last task (row 8 of 8) in the table.

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. assertion_results.evidence: Bookend tasks (non-documentation) lack required sections. task-1-create-feature-branch.md has Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements, but lacks 'Files to Modify' or 'Files to Create' and 'Implementation Notes'. task-8-merge-feature-branch.md similarly has Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements, but lacks 'Files to Modify' or 'Files to Create' and 'Implementation Notes'. Implementation tasks 2-6 all contain the full set of required sections. Documentation task 7 correctly includes Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements (exempt from Files to Modify/Create and Implementation Notes).

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: All convention references use the prescribed 'Applies:' format. Task 2: 'Applies: task creates `migration/src/m0002_advisory_status_enum/mod.rs` matching the convention's Rust migration file scope.' Task 3: 'Applies: task modifies `entity/src/advisory.rs` matching the convention's Rust entity file scope.' Task 4 has four convention entries each with correct 'Applies:' rationale. Task 5 has two convention entries with correct format. Task 6: 'Applies: task modifies `tests/api/advisory.rs` matching the convention's Rust test file scope.' No 'Not applicable' annotations appear anywhere. Bookend tasks (1, 8) and documentation task (7) correctly exclude conventions since they don't modify code files.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 40: '**Priority**: Critical -- inherited from parent Feature TC-9005, propagated to all created tasks via `additional_fields`'. The additional_fields JSON block (lines 46-49) includes '"priority": {"name": "Critical"}'. summary-comment.md line 38 confirms: '**Priority**: Critical -- propagated from Feature TC-9005 to all created tasks via `additional_fields`'.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md line 41: '**fixVersions**: RHTPA 2.0.0 -- inherited from parent Feature TC-9005, propagated to all created tasks via `additional_fields` (fixVersion scope defaults to "both" -- no `Jira Field Defaults` override present in CLAUDE.md)'. The additional_fields JSON block includes '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 2.0.0"}]'. summary-comment.md line 39 confirms: '**fixVersions**: RHTPA 2.0.0 -- propagated from Feature TC-9005 to all created tasks via `additional_fields` (fixVersion scope defaults to "both"; no `Jira Field Defaults` override configured in CLAUDE.md)'.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists and contains '## Inherited Field Values' section (lines 37-49) documenting Priority: Critical and fixVersions: RHTPA 2.0.0 with propagation details. impact-map.md also contains '## Field Inheritance' section (lines 38-51) with the same inherited values and the additional_fields JSON block applied to each task.
